sources.entry: Android tool for Mac - One-click screenshots, video recordings, app installation for iOS and Android

summary.one_liner: A Mac app that bundles common Android designer and developer tasks, such as screenshots, screen recordings, APK sideloading and bug reports, into one-click actions across all connected devices.
summary.what_it_does: Android Tool is a macOS app for working with Android devices connected to a Mac. It takes screenshots and screen videos from one or all connected devices in one click, and outputs both mp4 and animated gif for screen recordings. It installs (sideloads) APK files without the Play Store, and double-clicking an APK on disk opens the app to choose a target device. It can also take bug reports and run user-supplied bash scripts from a scripts folder against a selected device or all devices. The README says no Android or iOS SDK is required. It lists iOS features as well, but the README gives no detail on them.
use_cases: Take Android screenshots from a Mac
Record Android screen video as mp4 or gif
Sideload APK files without the Play Store
Install apps on multiple connected devices at once
Run custom bash scripts on connected devices
how_to_run: Download the latest AndroidTool.app from the README's download link
Copy AndroidTool.app to your Applications folder
Or install with Homebrew: brew cask install androidtool
notable: One-click screenshots and screen recordings across all devices connected to the Mac
Sideloads APKs by double-clicking them in Finder
Outputs both mp4 and animated gif from screen recordings
User-extensible through a scripts folder with an example that targets the selected device
caveats: Requires macOS 10.9 Mavericks or newer for Android features and 10.10 Yosemite for iOS features, per the README
Android 4.4 or newer is needed for screen recording and Android 4.3 or newer for screenshots
README does not state the project's maintenance status
keywords: share android screen gif in docs
